newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends slightly lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends slightly lower in thin trade.

text.p: June 20 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 99.08 99.10

The benchmark three-month December euroyen futures contract settled slightly lower in lethargic Friday Tokyo trade, with activity dampened as operators refrained from taking out fresh positions ahead of a host of upcoming events over the next week.
Although December crawled as high as 99.09 in afternoon trade, the emergence of profit-taking took it down again. It settled at 99.08, with turnover of 15,505 contracts.
Turnover on the March contract overwhelmed that of December in overnight trade and in Tokyo as well, with a benchmark shift imminent should this take place again on Monday, traders said.
The March moved from 98.83 to 98.87 and finally settled at 98.85, with turnover of 26,296.
Traders said this impending change was having little impact on trade, although one said speculative buying of March had been detected in morning trade due to December's immobility.
But the real inhibiting factor was apparently wariness about trading before upcoming events, starting with the G7 summit due to start later today and extending into next week.

Aside from the summit, the lineup also includes bond auctions next week, the release of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) "tankan" survey on June 25, and Japanese consumer price and employment data due out on Friday.

"It's actually virtually impossible at this point to predict what next week's moves will be like. First of all we have to see what happens with the dollar after the summit," one city bank dealer said.
He added that while it may take a while for the market to come to a consensus about direction, once they do the key contract could well move as much as 20 ticks.

Little impact was detected from comments out of Denver on Thursday from U.S. President Bill Clinton, who voiced concern to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about Japan's rising trade surplus, while U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said the U.S. will not dictate to Japan on deregulation, but will negotiate.

The market also shrugged off figures showing that Japan's diffusion index of leading economic indicators stood at 5.6 on a scale of 100 in April, down below 50 for the fourth consecutive month in April. Coincident indicators were at 10.0, below 50 for the first time in eight months.

Most traders said that movements were confined mainly to book-squaring. "The market came into Tokyo trade almost squared already, and after a little flurry in the morning to take care of the remaining positions, there has been very little activity at all," the city bank dealer said.
Overnight call money was being traded mostly at 0.49 percent, against 0.51 percent on Thursday, after the BOJ conducted a slightly more generous operation than expected.
The central bank drained 100 billion yen from the market against a net 200 billion yen in surplus. Many in the market had expected a drainage of 200 billion yen.

In the longer end of the money market, around 40 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposits (CDs) were issued at 0.60 percent, while around 60 billion of two-month CDs were issued at 0.59 percent. Both were unchanged from Thursday, when 50 billion yen of three-month CDs and 60 billion yen of two-month CDs were issued.
No one-month CDs were issued.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, the three-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.53/1.57 percent against 1.51/1/55 percent on Thursday.
